name: Ankle Dorsiflexion Stretch
description: The ankle dorsiflexion stretch is a targeted mobility drill that improves the range of motion of the ankle into dorsiflexion — the movement of bringing the top of the foot toward the shin. Restricted dorsiflexion is one of the most common mobility limitations in athletes and gym-goers, contributing to limitations in squatting depth, running mechanics, and landing biomechanics. The knee-to-wall version provides a reliable, measurable way to assess and progressively improve dorsiflexion range.

execution.starting_position: Stand facing a wall with one foot approximately 10 cm from the base of the wall.
execution.setup_instructions: No equipment needed. Use a wall, rack, or any stable vertical surface. A tape measure or ruler can be used to track progress over time.
steps: Step 1: Place one foot 5–15 cm from the base of the wall with toes pointing straight at the wall.
Step 2: Keeping the heel flat on the floor, drive the knee toward the wall, aiming to touch the wall with the knee.
Step 3: Keep the knee tracking over the second toe — do not let it cave inward.
Step 4: If the knee touches the wall with the heel flat, move the foot further back and repeat.
Step 5: Find the maximum distance where the heel can remain flat while the knee touches the wall. Hold 5–10 seconds at that position.
Step 6: Perform 10–15 repetitions or hold for 30–60 seconds per side.
execution.breathing_instructions: Breathe normally throughout. On each exhale, gently drive the knee a little further toward the wall.
common_mistakes: Lifting the heel — this defeats the purpose of the stretch
Letting the knee cave inward medially — always keep the knee tracking over the second toe
Moving too fast — this is a mobility drill, not a ballistic movement
safety_considerations: If sharp pain occurs in the ankle joint (not muscle tightness), stop and consult a clinician
This drill is safe for most populations and is frequently prescribed in physical therapy
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Track the foot-to-wall distance where you can maintain heel contact. A common benchmark is 10 cm or more. Progress by gradually increasing this distance over weeks.
execution.tempo_recommendations: 10–15 reps × 3 sets per side, or hold 30–60 seconds × 2–3 rounds.
coaching_cues: Heel stays glued to the floor the entire time
Drive the knee straight forward over the toes
Feel the stretch in the calf, not pain in the joint
